title: Creating natural spoken audio · Level 3
slo: Describe the stages that convert written text into natural-sounding speech.

exercises.question_text: Which stage changes raw recognized text into easier-to-read text?

options.rationale: Post-processing refines decoded recognition output for people to read. It can add capitalization, punctuation, and number formatting.

options.error_type: Confuses recognition cleanup with TTS input preparation
options.rationale: Text normalization prepares written input before it is spoken. It does not clean a completed transcription.
options.better_fit: Use text normalization when abbreviations, dates, symbols, or numbers need pronounceable spoken forms.

options.error_type: Confuses selecting words with formatting output
options.rationale: Beam search chooses a likely word sequence from competing possibilities. It occurs before readable formatting is added.
options.better_fit: Use beam search when selecting the best transcription hypothesis.

options.error_type: Confuses sound prediction with text cleanup
options.rationale: Phoneme prediction concerns speech sounds from audio features. It is not a cleanup step for recognized words.
options.better_fit: Use phoneme prediction during acoustic modeling of spoken audio.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Post-processing improves decoded recognition output with readable formatting.

exercises.question_text: Which elements are part of prosody? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Pitch contours are rising and falling pitch patterns. They contribute to speech expression.
Pauses separate phrases and aid comprehension. They are a prosody element.
Stress patterns indicate which syllables or words receive emphasis. They shape delivery.

options.error_type: Confuses delivery patterns with recognition metadata
options.rationale: Word timestamps identify when recognized words occurred. They are not vocal delivery patterns.
options.better_fit: Use word-level timestamps to locate words in a recognition transcription.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These features shape rhythm and expression.

exercises.question_text: Confidence scoring can flag low-confidence words for human review.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: An uncertain clinical word could be missed during review.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Confidence scoring identifies words the recognition result is less certain about so a person can check them.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Confidence scoring estimates certainty and can highlight words needing review.

exercises.question_text: A lexicon is a pronunciation dictionary used during linguistic analysis.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A familiar word’s pronunciation could be treated as if no reference existed.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A lexicon stores word pronunciations for linguistic analysis.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Linguistic analysis uses lexicons to look up pronunciations.

exercises.question_text: What can text normalization expand before speech is generated? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Text normalization expands abbreviations into pronounceable words. “Dr.” can become “Doctor.”
Dates can be converted into spoken forms during normalization. This prevents unnatural readings of date characters.
Normalization handles symbols such as “$” and “@.” It changes them into spoken forms.

options.error_type: Confuses text preparation with audio generation
options.rationale: Audio waveforms are generated later in speech synthesis. Text normalization works with written input.
options.better_fit: Use waveform generation after phonemes and prosody have produced acoustic features.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These written forms are expanded so they can be pronounced naturally.

options.rationale: Prosody determines rhythm, stress, intonation, timing, and emphasis. It decides how phonemes are said.
Letters and phonemes are handled during linguistic analysis and G2P. Prosody shapes delivery after sounds are known.
options.better_fit: Use G2P when mapping written letters to phonemes.

options.error_type: Confuses synthesis prosody with recognition decoding
options.rationale: Determining spoken words is recognition decoding. Prosody shapes synthesis output.
options.better_fit: Use decoding to select a recognition transcription.

options.rationale: Symbol expansion is text normalization. Prosody sets delivery patterns from linguistic context.
options.better_fit: Use text normalization to expand symbols before speech generation.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Prosody controls expressive delivery through pitch, stress, timing, and pauses.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence would blur the input, conversion, and output of pronunciation mapping.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with normalized text, then show G2P mapping it to phonemes.

exercises.correct_answer: Normalized text is mapped by G2P to phonemes
exercises.explanation: G2P acts on normalized written forms and maps their graphemes to phonemes.

exercises.question_text: Which are neural vocoder architectures? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: WaveNet is a neural vocoder architecture. It generates audio samples from acoustic representations.
WaveGlow is a neural vocoder architecture. It belongs to waveform generation in speech synthesis.
HiFi-GAN is a neural vocoder architecture. It can create raw audio waveforms.

options.error_type: Confuses recognition features with synthesis vocoding
options.rationale: MFCC is an audio feature representation used in recognition. It does not generate audio.
options.better_fit: Use MFCCs to represent captured audio before acoustic modeling.

exercises.explanation: Correct. WaveNet, WaveGlow, and HiFi-GAN are neural vocoders.

exercises.question_text: Rhythm, stress, and intonation in speech are called ___.

parts.text: Rhythm, stress, and intonation in speech are called

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The narration could be treated as a text-preparation or waveform task.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Prosody controls rhythm, stress, and intonation.

exercises.explanation: Prosody is the set of delivery patterns involving pitch, timing, emphasis, and pauses.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The process could try to create audio before its acoustic representation exists.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Follow the dependency from phonemes and prosody to mel-spectrograms, then waveforms.

exercises.correct_answer: Phonemes and prosody create mel-spectrograms then a vocoder creates waveforms
exercises.explanation: Phonemes and prosody guide mel-spectrogram generation; the vocoder then creates waveform audio.

parts.text: Changing spoken “three p m” into “3 PM” is called

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The time would remain in a spoken-word form in the written record.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Inverse text normalization moves spoken forms back to formatted writing after recognition.

exercises.explanation: Inverse text normalization converts spoken forms in recognition output into conventional written forms.

exercises.question_text: What is the main purpose of text normalization?

options.rationale: Text normalization changes nonstandard written forms into speakable forms. It prepares input before speech generation.

options.error_type: Confuses synthesis input with recognition output
options.rationale: Finished recognition output is cleaned during post-processing. Normalization acts before speech is created.
options.better_fit: Use post-processing to add punctuation and capitalization after recognition.

options.rationale: Choosing among word sequences is decoding. Normalization expands written forms for pronunciation.
options.better_fit: Use decoding when selecting the transcription that fits the audio.

options.error_type: Confuses text preparation with acoustic modeling
options.rationale: Phoneme probabilities come from acoustic modeling of audio. Text normalization works on written input.
options.better_fit: Use acoustic modeling to predict likely phonemes from audio features.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Normalization turns written forms into forms that can be pronounced naturally.
